title: CAG-audited Delhi Street Lighting Modernisation — CWG-2010
source_name: Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG)

audit_findings.label: High-cost imported luminary procurement
audit_findings.finding: CAG reported avoidable extra expenditure of Rs. 31.07 crore across PWD, MCD and NDMC on imported luminaries. The audit recorded identical technical specifications for imported and indigenous luminaries and found substantially higher procurement prices for imported units.

audit_findings.label: Competition restricted by tender conditions
audit_findings.finding: CAG reported tenders restricted to manufacturers of international repute and higher financial eligibility, restricting competition.

audit_findings.label: Bidder qualification anomaly
audit_findings.finding: CAG reported that SpaceAge was initially declared disqualified and later declared qualified after reassessment following an appeal.

audit_findings.label: Suspected post-tender bid alteration
audit_findings.finding: CAG reported suspected post-tender alteration of bids in MCD Phase-I and Phase-II, with quoted amounts enhanced by Rs. 3.63 crore and Rs. 3.34 crore respectively.

key_evidence.label: Project scale
key_evidence.value: Around 800 km of Delhi roads; tendered cost Rs. 286 crore

key_evidence.label: Price example
key_evidence.value: Keselec-Schreder Ambar-3: Rs. 15,160 in PWD as indigenous vs Rs. 32,000 in MCD as imported

key_evidence.label: Audit conclusion
key_evidence.value: Avoidable extra expenditure of Rs. 31.07 crore across three agencies

investigator_next_checks: Open the CAG chapter and trace each finding to the underlying tender, invoice and approval records.
Compare the specifications used for imported and indigenous luminaries.
Verify the documented justification and cost-benefit analysis for imported luminaries.
Check original MCD tender files against the altered bid values noted by CAG.
verification_notes: This is a real CAG-audited case reconstructed as an investigation profile. The audit findings are historical and source-backed; SENTRY should present them as evidence-backed signals/findings, not as a new allegation. Physical verification quantities are demo mission settings and must be labelled as such.

title: CAG-audited Dhanbad LED Street Light Installation
source_name: Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG)
category: Audited procurement + installation case / LED street lighting

audit_findings.label: Specification reduction without price reduction
audit_findings.finding: CAG reported that MC Dhanbad reduced wattage, LED efficiency and ingress protection in the tender specifications from the model estimate without reducing the price.

audit_findings.label: Large non-functionality in physical verification
audit_findings.finding: Of 237 LED lights jointly physically verified, CAG found 171 (72 per cent) either non-functional or functioning improperly.

audit_findings.label: Unfruitful expenditure
audit_findings.finding: CAG reported that payment of Rs. 0.79 crore on the 171 lights that could not be put to use or were functioning improperly was unfruitful.

key_evidence.label: Supply/payment
key_evidence.value: 795 lights supplied till June 2016; Rs. 3.63 crore paid

key_evidence.label: Physical verification
key_evidence.value: 237 lights checked; 171 (72%) non-functional or improperly functioning

key_evidence.label: Audit impact
key_evidence.value: Rs. 0.79 crore expenditure on the 171 lights was reported as unfruitful

investigator_next_checks: Compare the model estimate specifications with the tendered specifications.
Review contractor responsibilities for feeder pillar, transformer connection, timer, earthing and LED panel defects.
Verify the joint physical verification records and site-wise asset list.
Reconcile supplied quantity, payment records and functional status.
Check warranty-period corrective action and completion/acceptance records.
verification_notes: This is a real CAG-audited procurement-and-installation case reconstructed as an investigation profile. The physical-verification figures are historical audit evidence. Any live rover mismatch shown in the demo must be explicitly labelled as a current simulated field mission, not as a new measurement of the historical site.
